content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on why students should be encouraged to develop effective communication skills. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: why students should be encouraged to develop effective communication skills

modelEssay.title: Why Students Should Develop Effective Communication Skills
modelEssay.content: Effective communication skills are indispensable in today's society, and students should be encouraged to develop these skills for several compelling reasons. Firstly, good communication skills can enhance one's academic performance. Students who can articulate their thoughts clearly are better able to participate in class discussions, ask insightful questions, and collaborate on group projects. Moreover, effective communication is crucial in the professional world. Employers value individuals who can communicate their ideas persuasively and work well in teams. Additionally, strong communication skills can lead to better interpersonal relationships. Being able to express oneself and understand others fosters empathy and cooperation, which are vital for both personal and professional success. In conclusion, equipping students with effective communication skills is essential for their personal growth, academic achievement, and future career prospects.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：强调有效沟通技能在当今社会的重要性，并提出学生应该被鼓励发展这些技能的观点。
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：具体阐述有效沟通技能在学术表现、职业发展和人际关系中的作用。
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：总结有效沟通技能对学生个人成长、学术成就和未来职业前景的重要性。

运用了'Firstly, Moreover, Additionally'等连接词来组织文章结构

transcript.text: This is unbelievable, unlike any video game I've ever played before.

transcript.text: It's so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你是怎么听说这个驾驶模拟器的？

transcript.text: My brother introduced it to me last year.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我哥哥去年介绍给我的。

transcript.text: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我惊讶地发现它如此具有教育意义和逼真。

transcript.text: It's called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它叫做《欧洲卡车模拟器》，但他们也有其他版本，比如美国版等。

transcript.text: I was really drawn to the scenery.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我确实被风景所吸引。

transcript.text: The routes go through parts of the country you don't normally see as a tourist.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 路线穿越了作为游客通常不会看到的地区。

transcript.text: Yeah, I can see that.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，我看得出来。

transcript.text: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 看起来很简单，只是将货物从A点运到B点，从一个城市开到另一个城市。

transcript.text: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但我真的很欣赏游戏中融入的所有细节。

transcript.text: It's even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它甚至让我对物流业和道路上的交通有了新的认识。

transcript.text: I completely agree.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我完全同意。

transcript.text: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我哥哥还让我看了些有人在线直播游戏的视频。

transcript.text: It was fascinating to watch, really.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 看起来真的很迷人。

transcript.text: This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这个人开车非常小心，遵守所有路标和交通规则。

transcript.text: Such a contrast to most violent games.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 与大多数暴力游戏形成鲜明对比。

transcript.text: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 老实说，玩这个游戏激发了我进一步了解这个行业的兴趣。

transcript.text: I've read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我读过一些文章，讲述自动驾驶卡车可能很快上市，并可能对货物物流产生巨大影响。

transcript.text: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it's amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 考虑到驾驶这些大型车辆所需的一切，我们可能很快拥有那种技术真是令人惊讶。

transcript.text: Huh, I've gone one step further.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 呵，我更进一步。

transcript.text: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我报名参加了安全驾驶课程，以提高我的现实驾驶技能。

transcript.text: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在某种程度上，我觉得与班上其他学生相比，我有一个领先优势。

transcript.text: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practice already.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 玩这个游戏已经给了我一些操作练习。

transcript.text: I'm not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real-life situations, but if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I'd say that's a positive outcome.

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: How do you like being self-employed?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你觉得做自由职业者感觉如何？

transcript.text: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated, as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 显然有不少好处，尽管我似乎没有预期的那份自由，因为我好像就是无法拒绝工作邀请。

transcript.text: And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且独自工作时，我发现有时单靠金钱并不足以提供动力。

transcript.text: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 自从你开始为自己工作后，也有过类似经历吗？

transcript.text: Sometimes, yes.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有时候是的。

transcript.text: Unlike the rest of the workforce, who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 与其他在职者不同——他们有管理者在感到懒散或无聊时激发动力，而我们自由职业者工作时没有经理来鼓舞士气。

transcript.text: There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没有人提供赞扬或发起协作，没有人能更好地利用我们的兴趣和才能。

transcript.text: That's a fact.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这是事实。

transcript.text: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 当然，并非所有管理者都具备这样的意识和关怀。

transcript.text: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且也并非所有管理者都懂得如何激励人。

transcript.text: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 尽管如此，身边有个管理者至少意味着，在你精力与注意力开始枯竭时，他们可能足够体谅地为你留心。

transcript.text: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我最看重的激励因素是自主性。

transcript.text: I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我已经学会了不为了满足每个客户的请求而全天候工作，以免牺牲我所珍视的自主权。

transcript.text: Yes, I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independents.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，我需要提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式是为了独立性。

transcript.text: I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours, and so on.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我并不怀念永久性全职工作中令我不喜欢的方面，比如办公室政治、工作不稳定、工时不灵活等等。

transcript.text: I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise, though.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过，我倒是不介意以书面形式得到更多一点的赞扬。

transcript.text: Praise which is on the record.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 有记录可查的赞扬。

transcript.text: That'll come with time.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这会随着时间推移而来的。

transcript.text: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction, engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人际联系必然会通过人际互动来培养，比如与客户打交道、获得书面证明和推荐信、之后与客户保持联系。

transcript.text: These are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你会发现这些事情会在适当的时候到来，并为你提供动力。

transcript.text: You're right.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你说得对。

transcript.text: That's an area I do need to put some more effort into, building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在这方面我确实需要投入更多努力，与聘请我服务的人建立更紧密的关系。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 篇章1。

transcript.text: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there's little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
transcript.translation: 天气是我们生活中一个恒定因素，但关于它如何影响企业的营销研究很少。

transcript.text: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
transcript.translation: 现在，一项新研究揭示了晴朗和下雪的天气条件如何影响消费者行为。

transcript.text: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
transcript.translation: 这些天气条件促使消费者在脑海中想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。

transcript.text: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
transcript.translation: 这导致消费者对这些产品给予更高的价值。

transcript.text: That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，他们愿意为这些产品支付更多的钱。

transcript.text: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
transcript.translation: 但这种关联只存在于与户外活动相关的产品中。

transcript.text: How does this work?
transcript.translation: 这是如何运作的？

transcript.text: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
transcript.translation: 研究人员举了一个沙滩巾的例子。

transcript.text: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself.
transcript.translation: 在晴朗的日子里，看到该产品的消费者不仅仅是在看毛巾本身。

transcript.text: They are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
transcript.translation: 他们很可能想象自己躺在阳光下的毛巾上。

transcript.text: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumer's mind.
transcript.translation: 这种使用毛巾的思维画面增加了产品在消费者心目中的价值。

transcript.text: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
transcript.translation: 研究人员提出了以下假设来解释他们的发现。

transcript.text: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
transcript.translation: 他们认为这种思维画面在阳光和雪天有效，因为这些天气条件与户外活动有积极关联。

transcript.text: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
transcript.translation: 这种效应在雨天天气中看不到。

transcript.text: Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
transcript.translation: 研究人员断言，这是因为雨天所能进行的活动不多。

transcript.text: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather and not for any activities.
transcript.translation: 大多数与雨相关的产品，如雨伞，仅用于防雨，而非用于任何活动。

transcript.text: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
transcript.translation: 研究人员相信，在线销售多种产品的公司能从这项研究提供的见解中受益最多。

transcript.text: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price those products.
transcript.translation: 在线卖家经常使用复杂的数学公式来决定推荐哪些产品以及如何为这些产品定价。

transcript.text: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
transcript.translation: 整合更多关于天气的数据将使他们能够做出更好的决策。

transcript.text: This could bolster sales.
transcript.translation: 这可能会促进销售。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 段落2。

transcript.text: Setting the office air conditioning at about 22 degrees Celsius has become standard practice across the world.
transcript.translation: 将办公室空调设置在约22摄氏度已成为全球的标准做法。

transcript.text: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation, and air conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
transcript.translation: 全球众多关于供暖、通风和空调的指南声称，办公室绩效在22度时达到峰值。

transcript.text: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices, but recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
transcript.translation: 许多人确实在空调办公室中从炎热的夏季高温中获得缓解，但最近的研究挑战了凉爽办公室更高效的普遍观点。

transcript.text: The reality is more complex.
transcript.translation: 现实更为复杂。

transcript.text: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air conditioning and productivity.
transcript.translation: 研究人员对所有与空调和生产力相关的研究进行了综述。

transcript.text: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
transcript.translation: 他们发现，即使在盛夏，22度可能也有点冷。

transcript.text: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees, and people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
transcript.translation: 对于穿着典型夏季服装的人来说，最佳范围在23到26度之间，只要他们能调整服装和期望，甚至可以容忍超出这个舒适区的温度。

transcript.text: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air conditioning up.
transcript.translation: 事实上，即使在非常热的日子里，调高空调温度也是合理的。

transcript.text: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot, but there is a range of at least 3 to 4 degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
transcript.translation: 人们常常追求一个最佳温度，当人们感到热时这是可以理解的，但至少有一个3到4度的范围不会产生任何不利影响。

transcript.text: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
transcript.translation: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能会对空调产生心理依赖。

transcript.text: If they are used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures, but the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
transcript.translation: 如果他们习惯了空调环境，他们往往倾向于较低的温度，但研究发现几乎所有人都会适应新温度。

transcript.text: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
transcript.translation: 只有在温度范围的极端端点，人们的生产力才会受到影响。

transcript.text: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
transcript.translation: 心理学研究倾向于将独处描绘为一种负面体验。

transcript.text: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
transcript.translation: 20世纪70年代和90年代的研究表明，与与他人在一起相比，人们在独处时感到更不快乐。

transcript.text: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
transcript.translation: 然而，一篇新论文提出了独处的一种替代观点，即独处可以是积极的。

transcript.text: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
transcript.translation: 让我们先来看一下早期的研究。

transcript.text: It had a couple of shortcomings.
transcript.translation: 它有几个缺点。

transcript.text: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
transcript.translation: 首先，它在积极到消极的量表上测量情绪，忽略了积极和消极情绪可能独立波动的可能性。

transcript.text: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
transcript.translation: 此外，它将情绪简单地归类为积极或消极。

transcript.text: It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
transcript.translation: 它没有考虑到情绪会以不同程度唤起我们，并且积极和消极情绪都能强烈或轻微地唤起我们。

transcript.text: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high arousal or low arousal.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，无论是积极还是消极，情绪都可以是高唤醒或低唤醒的。

transcript.text: High arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
transcript.translation: 高唤醒情绪包括积极方面的兴奋或消极方面的愤怒，而低唤醒情绪包括积极方面的平静感或消极方面的孤独感。

transcript.text: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
transcript.translation: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺点。

transcript.text: Researchers began with a simple study.
transcript.translation: 研究人员从一项简单的研究开始。

transcript.text: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity and measured how this solitude influenced their emotional state.
transcript.translation: 他们要求参与者独自坐15分钟，不进行任何活动，并测量这种独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。

transcript.text: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high arousal emotions.
transcript.translation: 这项实验旨在确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。

transcript.text: It looked at positive emotions, such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions, including being scared or distressed.
transcript.translation: 它考察了积极情绪，如兴奋或感兴趣，以及消极情绪，包括害怕或苦恼。

transcript.text: The results were clear.
transcript.translation: 结果很明确。

transcript.text: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
transcript.translation: 独处15分钟后，参与者在这两种情绪上都表现出减少。

transcript.text: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low arousal emotions.
transcript.translation: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。

transcript.text: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad, or lonely.
transcript.translation: 这些包括积极和消极情绪，如感到平静、放松、悲伤或孤独。

transcript.text: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
transcript.translation: 那项实验发现，所有这些情绪都因独处时间而增加。

transcript.text: Thus, it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
transcript.translation: 因此，似乎过去对独处的描绘是错误的。

transcript.text: It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
transcript.translation: 它没有简单的情绪效应，可以被描述为好或坏。

transcript.text: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
transcript.translation: 相反，它改变了我们内在体验的强度。

transcript.text: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
transcript.translation: 它放大安静的情绪，但减弱强烈感受的强度。

transcript.text: It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
transcript.translation: 值得澄清的是，这些发现涉及相对较短的独处时间。

transcript.text: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
transcript.translation: 这与长期孤独不同。

transcript.text: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，后者与各种负面身体和心理效应相关。

transcript.text: How can people benefit from being alone?
transcript.translation: 人们如何能从独处中受益？

transcript.text: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
transcript.translation: 这里的发现表明，人们可以利用独处来调节他们的情绪。

transcript.text: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
transcript.translation: 独处可以帮助我们在兴奋后变得平静，在愤怒事件后恢复平静，或 simply feel at peace.

transcript.text: In 1984, the World Chess Championships was called off abruptly due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
transcript.translation: 1984年，世界国际象棋锦标赛因一名争夺冠军的选手身体虚弱而突然取消。

transcript.text: He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
transcript.translation: 他并非唯一经历这项运动极端体能影响的人。

transcript.text: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
transcript.translation: 据报道，精英选手一天可燃烧高达6,000卡路里，这数字惊人。

transcript.text: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
transcript.translation: 这是否意味着更努力思考是减肥的简单途径？

transcript.text: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20-25% of the overall energy.
transcript.translation: 嗯，当身体休息时，我们知道大脑会消耗高达总能量的20-25%，这令人惊讶。

transcript.text: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
transcript.translation: 这种利用水平实际上使大脑成为身体中最耗能的器官，尽管它仅占总体重的2%。

transcript.text: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn?
transcript.translation: 那么，我们让这个器官工作得越多，燃烧的卡路里就越多吗？

transcript.text: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
transcript.translation: 技术上，答案是肯定的，对于认知困难的任务。

transcript.text: What counts as a difficult mental task varies between individuals, but generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
transcript.translation: 什么算作困难的心理任务因人而异，但通常，它可以被描述为大脑无法轻松使用先前学到的常规解决的事情，或条件不断变化的任务。

transcript.text: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack, because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
transcript.translation: 然而，深度思考不会燃烧掉吃含糖零食获得的卡路里，因为相对于大脑巨大的总能量消耗（用于众多任务），仅仅更努力思考所需的能量实际上相对微小。

transcript.text: We're unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
transcript.translation: 我们对大脑能量消耗的大部分过程是无意识的。

transcript.text: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
transcript.translation: 许多这种活动与有意识的活动无关，如学习唱歌或弹吉他。

transcript.text: The brain is able to allocate blood and thus energy to particular regions that are being active at that point, but the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
transcript.translation: 大脑能够将血液和能量分配到特定区域，这些区域在那时是活跃的，但大脑中的总能量可用性被认为是恒定的。

transcript.text: So while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
transcript.translation: 因此，当我们执行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量使用可能会显著增加，但就整个大脑的能量预算总体而言，这些活动不会显著改变它。

transcript.text: So why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
transcript.translation: 那么，为什么这位国际象棋冠军变得太瘦而无法参加比赛？

transcript.text: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
transcript.translation: 普遍共识是，这主要归因于压力和食物摄入减少，而不是精神疲惫。

transcript.text: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
transcript.translation: 长时间保持身体为行动做好准备是非常消耗能量的。

transcript.text: If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally, then you might lose weight.
transcript.translation: 如果你不能像通常那样频繁或大量进食，那么你可能会减肥。

transcript.text: Tell me about yourself.
transcript.translation: 介绍一下你自己。

transcript.text: May seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
transcript.translation: 这似乎是一个简单的面试问题，但这个问题的开放式性质常常让求职者不知从何说起。

transcript.text: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate's communication skills, so it's important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
transcript.translation: 这个常见问题实际上是对求职者沟通能力的关键考验，所以不要给出未经准备的回答或搞砸它很重要。

transcript.text: Tell me about yourself is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
transcript.translation: '介绍一下你自己'通常是职业教练在提供面试指导时准备的第一个问题。

transcript.text: It's the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
transcript.translation: 这是候选人掌控叙述、以真正对听众重要的方式讲述自己故事的机会。

transcript.text: It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
transcript.translation: 要回答好这个问题需要努力和广泛的准备。

transcript.text: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their resume, so they don't need to repeat the information.
transcript.translation: 当一个人去面试时，面试官可能已经看过他们的简历，所以他们不需要重复这些信息。

transcript.text: But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their resume.
transcript.translation: 但大多数人会这样做，因为他们的本能是背诵简历上已有的内容。

transcript.text: It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
transcript.translation: 求职者在两个关键方面做好功课很重要。

transcript.text: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
transcript.translation: 首先，他们不只是在告诉别人关于自己的一个事实。

transcript.text: They're telling a story, and stories take work to create.
transcript.translation: 他们在讲述一个故事，而故事需要花功夫来创作。

transcript.text: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they're proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
transcript.translation: 想出一个好的故事意味着要反思是什么让他们的职业成就值得骄傲，以及这些成就突出了哪些优势。

transcript.text: Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as, I'm smart, I work hard, and I get things done.
transcript.translation: 候选人不应该选择一个宽泛的优势来阐述，比如，我很聪明，我工作努力，我能完成任务。

transcript.text: To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends, or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
transcript.translation: 为了想出多个职业成就或不同面试问题的例子，求职者应该与他人交谈，尤其是了解他们的人，如伴侣、朋友或同事，这些人会提出与他们记忆中不同的故事。

transcript.text: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the opening.
transcript.translation: 其次，候选人应该知道这个开头事关重大。

transcript.text: What they really are asking you is, tell me why you are going to help me.
transcript.translation: 他们真正想问的是，告诉我你将如何帮助我。

transcript.text: If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
transcript.translation: 如果这个人是有准备的候选人，他们应该已经弄清楚了这些事情。

transcript.text: They've read the job description and researched the company on the internet.
transcript.translation: 他们已经阅读了职位描述并在网上研究了公司。

transcript.text: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish, and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
transcript.translation: 求职者应该关注的是公司在做什么，他们试图实现什么，以及是什么阻碍了他们实现这些目标。

transcript.text: How long should it take to answer?
transcript.translation: 回答应该花多长时间？

transcript.text: Around a minute.
transcript.translation: 大约一分钟。

transcript.text: That's about right for most people's attention spans.
transcript.translation: 这对大多数人的注意力集中时间来说是合适的。

transcript.text: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
transcript.translation: 不到一分钟可能显得仓促，而超过两分钟就会开始感觉更像演讲。

transcript.text: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
transcript.translation: 但回答的长度不是一门精确的科学，候选人需要保持他们的职业故事集中并针对听众进行调整。

questionGroups.title: Section A

paragraphs.text: Virtually every activity that entails or facilitates in-person human interaction seems to be in the midst of a total meltdown as the coronavirus outbreak erases Americans' desire to travel. Amtrak says bookings are down 50 percent and cancelations are up 300 percent. Hotels in San Francisco are experiencing __26__ rates between 70 and 80 percent. Broadway goes dark on Thursday night. Universities, now emptying their campuses, have never tried online learning on this __27__. White collar companies like Amazon, Apple, and the New York Times are asking employees to work from home for the __28__ future.
paragraphs.translation: 几乎每一个涉及或促进面对面人际互动的活动，似乎都因冠状病毒爆发抹去了美国人出行的意愿而正在经历彻底崩溃。Amtrak表示，预订量下降了50%，取消量上升了300%。旧金山酒店的空置率在70%到80%之间。百老汇在周四晚上熄灯。大学正在清空校园，从未尝试过如此大规模的在线学习。亚马逊、苹果和《纽约时报》等白领公司要求员工在可预见的未来在家工作。

paragraphs.text: But what happens after the coronavirus?
paragraphs.translation: 但冠状病毒之后会发生什么？

paragraphs.text: In some ways, the answer is All the old normal stuff. The pandemic will take lives, __29__ economies and destroy routines, but it will pass. Americans will never stop going to basketball games. They won't stop going on vacation. They'll meet to do business. No decentralizing technology so far—not telephones, not television, and not the internet—has dented that human desire to shake hands, despite technologists' __30__ to the contrary.
paragraphs.translation: 在某些方面，答案是所有旧有的正常事物。大流行将夺走生命、扼杀经济并破坏日常生活，但它会过去。美国人永远不会停止去看篮球赛。他们不会停止度假。他们会面谈生意。迄今为止，没有任何去中心化技术——无论是电话、电视还是互联网——削弱了人们握手的愿望，尽管技术专家的预测相反。

paragraphs.text: Yet there are real reasons to think that things will not return to the way they were last week. Small __31__ create small societal shifts; big ones change things for good. The New York transit strike of 1980 is __32__ with prompting several long-term changes in the city, including bus and bike lanes, and women wearing sports shoes to work. The Spanish flu pandemic of 1918 prompted the development of national health care in Europe.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，有真实理由认为事情不会恢复到上周的状态。细微的小事造成小的社会转变；大事则永久改变事物。1980年的纽约交通罢工被认为促成了该市的几个长期变化，包括公交车道和自行车道，以及女性穿运动鞋上班。1918年的西班牙流感大流行促使了欧洲国家医疗保健的发展。

paragraphs.text: Here and now, this might not even be a question of __33__. It's not clear that the cruise industry will __34__. Or that public transit won't go broke without __35__ assistance. The infrastructure might not even be in place to do what we were doing in 2019.
paragraphs.translation: 眼下，这甚至可能不是偏好问题。尚不清楚邮轮业能否存活。或者公共交通在没有联邦援助的情况下是否会破产。基础设施可能甚至无法支持我们在2019年所做的事。

questionGroups.title: Slow Hope

paragraphs.text: Our world is full of—mostly untold—stories of slow hope, driven by the idea that change is possible. They are 'slow' in their unfolding, and they are slow because they come with setbacks.
paragraphs.translation: 我们的世界充满了——大多是未被讲述的——缓慢希望的故事，这些故事受到变革可能的理念驱动。它们展开得很“缓慢”，之所以缓慢是因为它们伴随着挫折。

paragraphs.text: At the beginning of time—so goes the myth—humans suffered, shivering in the cold and dark until the titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods. Just as in the myth, technology—first fire and stone tools, and later farming, the steam engine and industry, fossil fuels, chemicals and nuclear power—has allowed us to alter and control the natural world. The myth also reminds us that these advances have come at a price: as a punishment for Prometheus' crime, the gods created Pandora, and they gave her a box filled with evils and curses. When Pandora's box was opened, it unleashed swarms of diseases and disasters upon humankind.
paragraphs.translation: 在时间之初——神话如此叙述——人类受苦，在寒冷和黑暗中发抖，直到巨人普罗米修斯从众神那里偷来了火。就像神话中一样，技术——最初是火和石器，后来是农业、蒸汽机和工业、化石燃料、化学品和核能——使我们能够改变和控制自然世界。神话也提醒我们，这些进步是有代价的：作为对普罗米修斯罪行的惩罚，众神创造了潘多拉，并给了她一个装满邪恶和诅咒的盒子。当潘多拉的盒子被打开时，它释放出成群的疾病和灾难降临在人类身上。

paragraphs.text: Today we can no longer ignore the ecological curses that we have released in our search for warmth and comfort. In engineering and exploiting and transforming our habitat, we have opened tens of thousands of Pandora's boxes. In recent decades, environmental threats have expanded beyond regional boundaries to have global reach and, most hauntingly, are multiplying at a dizzying rate. On a regular basis, we are reminded that we are running out of time. Year after year, faster and faster, consumption outpaces the biological capacity of our planet. Stories of accelerated catastrophe multiply. We fear the breakdown of the electric grid, the end of non-renewable resources, the expansion of deserts, the loss of islands, and the pollution of our air and water.
paragraphs.translation: 今天，我们再也无法忽视在追求温暖和舒适的过程中释放的生态诅咒。在工程化、开发和改造我们的栖息地的过程中，我们打开了成千上万个潘多拉的盒子。近几十年来，环境威胁已经超越了区域边界，具有全球范围，并且最令人不安的是，它们正以令人眩晕的速度倍增。我们经常被提醒，时间所剩无几。年复一年，越来越快，消耗超过了我们星球的生物承载能力。加速灾难的故事倍增。我们害怕电网崩溃、不可再生资源枯竭、沙漠扩张、岛屿消失以及空气和水的污染。

paragraphs.text: Acceleration is the signature of our time. Populations and economic activity grew slowly for much of human history. For thousands of years and well into early modern times, world economies saw no growth at all, but from around the mid-19th century and again, in particular, since the mid-20th, the real GDP has increased at an enormous speed, and so has human consumption. In the Middle Ages, households in Central Europe might have owned fewer than 30 objects on average; in 1900, this number had increased to 400, and in 2020 to 15,000. The acceleration of human production, consumption and travel has changed the animate and inanimate spheres. It has echoed through natural processes on which humans depend. Species extinction, deforestation, damming of rivers, occurrence of floods, the depletion of ozone, the degradation of ocean systems and many other areas are all experiencing acceleration. If represented graphically, the curve for all these changes looks rather like that well-known hockey stick: with little change over millennia and a dramatic upswing over the past decades.
paragraphs.translation: 加速是我们时代的标志。在人类历史的大部分时间里，人口和经济增长缓慢。数千年来直至近代早期，世界经济根本没有增长，但大约从19世纪中叶开始，特别是20世纪中叶以来，实际GDP以巨大速度增长，人类消费也是如此。在中世纪，中欧家庭平均可能拥有不到30件物品；1900年，这个数字增加到400件，2020年增加到15000件。人类生产、消费和旅行的加速改变了生命和非生命领域。它在人类所依赖的自然过程中产生了回响。物种灭绝、森林砍伐、河流筑坝、洪水发生、臭氧消耗、海洋系统退化以及许多其他领域都正在经历加速。如果用图形表示，所有这些变化的曲线看起来就像那个著名的曲棍球棒：千年间变化甚微，过去几十年急剧上升。

paragraphs.text: Some of today's narratives about the future seem to suggest that we too, like Prometheus, will be saved by a new Hercules, a divine engineer, someone who will mastermind, manoeuver and manipulate our planet. They suggest that geoengineering, cold fusion or faster-than-light spaceships might transcend once and for all the terrestrial constraints of rising temperatures, lack of energy, scarcity of food, lack of space, mountains of waste, polluted water—you name it.
paragraphs.translation: 今天关于未来的一些叙述似乎暗示，我们也会像普罗米修斯一样，被一个新的赫拉克勒斯、一个神圣的工程师、一个将策划、操纵和控制我们星球的人所拯救。他们暗示，地球工程、冷聚变或超光速飞船可能一劳永逸地超越地球的限制：气温上升、能源缺乏、食物短缺、空间不足、堆积如山的废物、污染的水——诸如此类。

paragraphs.text: Yet, if we envisage our salvation to come from a deus ex machina, from a divine engineer or a tech solutionist who will miraculously conjure up a new source of energy or another cure-all with revolutionary potency, we might be looking in the wrong place. The fact that we now imagine our planet as a whole does not mean that the 'rescue' of our planet will come with one big global stroke of genius and technology. It will more likely come by many small acts. Global heating and environmental degradation are not technological problems. They are highly political issues that are informed by powerful interests. Moreover, if history is a guide, then we can assume that any major transformations will once again be followed by a huge set of unintended consequences. So what do we do?
paragraphs.translation: 然而，如果我们设想拯救来自一个解围之神、一个神圣的工程师或一个技术解决方案主义者，他们奇迹般地变出一个新的能源或另一个具有革命效力的万能药，我们可能找错了地方。我们现在将地球视为一个整体，这一事实并不意味着对地球的“拯救”会来自一次全球性的天才和技术壮举。它更可能来自许多小的行动。全球变暖和环境退化不是技术问题。它们是受强大利益影响的高度政治化问题。此外，如果历史是指导，那么我们可以假设任何重大转型都将再次伴随着大量意想不到的后果。那么我们该怎么做？

paragraphs.text: This much is clear: we need to find ways that help us flatten the hockey-stick curves that reflect our ever-faster pace of ecological destruction and social acceleration. If we acknowledge that human manipulation of the Earth has been a destructive force, we can also imagine that human endeavours can help us build a less destructive world in the centuries to come. We might keep making mistakes. But we will also keep learning from our mistakes.
paragraphs.translation: 这一点很清楚：我们需要找到方法来帮助我们拉平那些反映我们日益加速的生态破坏和社会加速的曲棍球棒曲线。如果我们承认人类对地球的操纵是一种破坏性力量，我们也可以想象，人类的努力可以帮助我们在未来几个世纪中构建一个破坏性较小的世界。我们可能继续犯错误。但我们也将继续从错误中学习。

paragraphs.text: To counter the fears of disaster, we need to identify stories, visions and actions that work quietly towards a more hopeful future. Instead of one big narrative, a story of unexpected rescue by a larger-than-life hero, we need multiple stories: we need stories, not only of what Rob Nixon of Princeton University has called the 'slow violence' of environmental degradation (that is, the damage that is often invisible at first and develops slowly and gradually), but also stories of what I call 'slow hope'.
paragraphs.translation: 为了对抗对灾难的恐惧，我们需要识别那些悄然朝着更希望未来努力的故事、愿景和行动。我们需要多个故事，而不是一个大叙事，一个由超越凡人的英雄意外拯救的故事：我们需要故事，不仅关于普林斯顿大学的罗布·尼克松所说的环境退化的“缓慢暴力”（即起初往往不可见且缓慢渐进发展的损害），还有关于我称之为“缓慢希望”的故事。

paragraphs.text: We need an acknowledgement of our present ecological plight but also a language of positive change, visions of a better future. In The Principle of Hope (1954-1959), Ernst Bloch, one of the leading philosophers of the future, wrote that 'the most tragic form of loss... is the loss of the capacity to imagine that things could be different'. We need to identify visions and paths that will help us imagine a different, more just and more ecological world. Hope, for Bloch, has its starting point in fear, in uncertainty, and in crisis: it is a creative force that goes hand in hand with utopian 'wishful images'. It can be found in cultural products of the past—in fairy tales, in fiction, in architecture, in music, in the movies—in products of the human mind that contain 'the outlines of a better world'. What makes us 'authentic' as humans are visions of our 'potential'. In other words: living in hope makes us human.
paragraphs.translation: 我们需要承认我们当前的生态困境，但也需要一种积极改变的语言，一个更美好未来的愿景。在《希望原理》（1954-1959年）中，恩斯特·布洛赫，未来的主要哲学家之一，写道“最悲剧的损失形式……是失去想象事物可能不同的能力”。我们需要识别愿景和路径，帮助我们想象一个不同、更公正、更生态的世界。对布洛赫来说，希望的起点在于恐惧、不确定性和危机：它是一种与乌托邦“愿望形象”齐头并进的创造力量。它可以在过去的文化产品中找到——在童话故事、小说、建筑、音乐、电影中——在包含“更美好世界轮廓”的人类思维产品中。使我们作为人类“真实”的是我们对“潜力”的愿景。换句话说：生活在希望中使我们成为人类。

paragraphs.text: The power of small, grassroots movements to make changes that spread beyond their place of origin can be seen with the Slow Food movement, which began in Italy in the 1980s. The rise of fast-food restaurants after the Second World War produced a society full of cheap, industrially made foodstuffs. Under the leadership of Carlo Petrini, the Slow Food movement began in Piedmont, a region of Italy with a long history of poverty, violence and resistance to oppression. The movement transformed it into a region hospitable to traditional food cultures—based on native plants and breeds of animals. Today, Slow Food operates in more than 160 countries, poor and rich. It has given rise to thousands of projects around the globe, representing democratic politics, food sovereignty, biodiversity and sustainable agriculture.
paragraphs.translation: 小型草根运动做出超越其起源地变化的力量，可以从慢食运动中看出，该运动始于20世纪80年代的意大利。第二次世界大战后快餐店的兴起产生了充满廉价工业制造食品的社会。在卡洛·佩特里尼的领导下，慢食运动始于皮埃蒙特，一个有着长期贫困、暴力和反抗压迫历史的意大利地区。该运动将其转变为一个欢迎传统食品文化的地区——基于本土植物和动物品种。如今，慢食运动在160多个国家运营，涵盖贫穷和富裕国家。它在全球催生了数千个项目，代表了民主政治、粮食主权、生物多样性和可持续农业。

paragraphs.text: The unscrupulous commodification of food and the destruction of foodstuffs will continue to devastate soils, livelihoods and ecologies. Slow Food cannot undo the irresistible developments of the global food economy, but it can upset its theorists, it can 'speak differently', and it can allow people and their local food traditions and environments to flourish. Even in the United States—the fast-food nation—small farms and urban gardens are on the rise. The US Department of Agriculture provides an Urban Agriculture Toolkit and, according to a recent report, American millennials are changing their diets. In 2017, 6 per cent of US consumers claimed to be strictly vegetarian, up from 1 per cent in 2014. As more people realise that 'eating is an agricultural act', as the US poet and environmental activist Wendell Berry put it in 1989, slow hope advances.
paragraphs.translation: 食物的无耻商品化和食品的破坏将继续摧毁土壤、生计和生态系统。慢食运动无法逆转全球粮食经济的不可抗拒发展，但它可以扰乱其理论家，它可以“以不同方式言说”，它可以让人们及其当地食品传统和环境繁荣起来。即使在美国——这个快餐国家——小型农场和城市花园也在兴起。美国农业部提供了一个城市农业工具包，根据最近的一份报告，美国千禧一代正在改变他们的饮食。2017年，6%的美国消费者声称自己是严格的素食者，高于2014年的1%。随着越来越多的人认识到“吃是一种农业行为”，正如美国诗人和环保活动家温德尔·贝里在1989年所说，缓慢希望在推进。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Vegetarians would prefer not to be compelled to eat meat. Yet the reverse compulsion is hidden in the proposals for a new plant-based "planetary diet." Nowhere is this more visible than in India.
paragraphs.translation: 素食主义者宁愿不被迫吃肉。然而，反向的强制却隐藏在以植物为基础的“行星饮食”新提案中。这一点在印度表现得最为明显。

paragraphs.text: Earlier this year, the EAT-Lancet Commission released its global report on nutrition and called for a global shift to a more plant-based diet and for "substantially reducing consumption of animal source foods." In countries like India, that call could become a tool to aggravate an already tense political situation and stress already undernourished populations.
paragraphs.translation: 今年早些时候，EAT-兰塞特委员会发布了其全球营养报告，呼吁全球转向更以植物为基础的饮食，并“大幅减少动物源食品的消费”。在印度这样的国家，这种呼吁可能成为加剧本已紧张的政治局势和给本已营养不良的人口带来压力的工具。

paragraphs.text: The EAT report presumes that "traditional diets" in countries like India include little red meat, which might be consumed only on special occasions or as minor ingredients in mixed dishes.
paragraphs.translation: EAT报告假定，在印度等国家的“传统饮食”中很少包含红肉，红肉可能只在特殊场合或作为混合菜肴中的次要成分消费。

paragraphs.text: In India, however, there is a vast difference between what people would wish to consume and what they have to consume because of innumerable barriers around class, religion, culture, cost, geography, etc. Policymakers in India have traditionally pushed for a cereal-heavy "vegetarian diet" on a meat-eating population as a way of providing the cheapest sources of food.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，在印度，人们希望消费的东西和由于阶级、宗教、文化、成本、地理等无数障碍而必须消费的东西之间存在巨大差异。印度的决策者传统上推动以谷物为主的“素食饮食”针对肉食人口，作为提供最廉价食物来源的方式。

paragraphs.text: Currently, under an aggressive Hindu nationalist government, Muslims, Christians, disadvantaged classes and indigenous communities are being compelled to give up their traditional foods.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，在激进的印度教民族主义政府统治下，穆斯林、基督徒、弱势阶级和土著社区正被迫放弃他们的传统食物。

paragraphs.text: None of these concerns seem to have been appreciated by the EAT-Lancet Commission's representative, Brent Loken, who said "India has got such a great example" in sourcing protein from plants.
paragraphs.translation: 这些担忧似乎都没有被EAT-兰塞特委员会的代表布伦特·洛肯所重视，他说“印度在从植物中获取蛋白质方面提供了如此好的榜样”。

paragraphs.text: But how much of a model for the world is India's vegetarianism? In the Global Hunger Index 2019, the country ranks 102nd out of 117. Data from the National Family Health Survey indicate that only 10 percent of infants of 6 to 23 months are adequately fed.
paragraphs.translation: 但印度的素食主义在多大程度上能作为世界的榜样？在2019年全球饥饿指数中，该国在117个国家中排名第102位。全国家庭健康调查的数据表明，只有10%的6至23个月婴儿得到充分喂养。

paragraphs.text: Which is why calls for a plant-based diet modeled on India risk offering another whip with which to beat already vulnerable communities in developing countries.
paragraphs.translation: 这就是为什么呼吁以印度为模型的植物基础饮食，有提供另一条鞭子来打击发展中国家本已脆弱的社区的风险。

paragraphs.text: A diet directed at the affluent West fails to recognize that in low-income countries undernourished children are known to benefit from the consumption of milk and other animal source foods, improving cognitive functions, while reducing the prevalence of nutritional deficiencies as well as mortality.
paragraphs.translation: 一种针对富裕西方的饮食未能认识到，在低收入国家，营养不良的儿童因消费牛奶和其他动物源食品而受益，这能改善认知功能，同时减少营养缺乏的普遍性和死亡率。

paragraphs.text: EAT-Lancet claimed its intention was to "spark conversations" among all Indian stakeholders. Yet vocal critics of the food processing industry and food fortification strategies have been left out of the debate. But the most conspicuous omission may well be the absence of India's farmers.
paragraphs.translation: EAT-兰塞特声称其意图是“在印度所有利益相关者之间引发对话”。然而，食品加工行业和食品强化策略的直言不讳的批评者被排除在辩论之外。但最明显的遗漏可能正是印度农民的缺席。

paragraphs.text: The government, however, seems to have given the report a thumbs-up. Rather than addressing chronic hunger and malnutrition through an improved access to wholesome and nutrient-dense foods, the government is opening the door for company-dependent solutions, ignoring the environmental and economic cost, which will destroy local food systems. It's a model full of danger for future generations.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，政府似乎对报告表示赞同。政府不是通过改善对健康和高营养食物的获取来解决长期饥饿和营养不良问题，而是为依赖公司的解决方案敞开大门，忽视环境和经济成本，这将破坏当地食物系统。这是一个对未来充满危险的模式。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Back in 1964, in his book Games People Play, psychiatrist Eric Berne described a pattern of conversation he called "Why Don't You—Yes But", which remains one of the most irritating aspects of everyday social life. The person adopting the strategy is usually a chronic complainer. Something is terrible about their relationship, job, or other situation, and they moan about it ceaselessly, but find some excuse to dismiss any solution that's proposed. The reason, of course, is that on some level they don't want a solution; they want to be validated in their position that the world is out to get them. If they can "win" the game—dismissing every suggestion until their interlocutor gives up in annoyance—they get to feel pleasurably righteous in their resentments and excused from any obligation to change.
paragraphs.translation: 回溯到1964年，精神科医生埃里克·伯恩在他的著作《人们玩的游戏》中描述了一种他称之为“为什么你不—但是”的对话模式，这至今仍是日常社交生活中最令人恼火的方面之一。采用这种策略的人通常是一个习惯性的抱怨者。他们的关系、工作或其他情况有些糟糕，他们不停地抱怨，但找借口驳回任何提出的建议。当然，原因在于在某种程度上他们不想要解决方案；他们希望自己的立场得到认同，即世界在故意针对他们。如果他们能“赢”这场游戏——驳回每一个建议，直到对话者恼怒地放弃——他们就会在怨恨中感到愉快的正义感，并免除了任何改变的义务。

paragraphs.text: Part of the trouble here is the so-called responsibility/fault fallacy. When you're feeling hard done by—taken for granted by your partner, say, or obliged to work for a half-witted boss—it's easy to become attached to the position that it's not your job to address the matter, and that doing so would be an admission of fault. But there's a confusion here. For example, if I were to discover a newborn at my front door, it wouldn't be my fault, but it most certainly would be my responsibility. There would be choices to make, and no possibility of avoiding them, since trying to ignore the matter would be a choice. The point is that what goes for the baby on the doorstep is true in all cases: even if the other person is 100% in the wrong, there's nothing to be gained, long-term, from using this as a justification to evade responsibility.
paragraphs.translation: 部分问题在于所谓的责任/过错谬误。当你感到被亏待时——比如被伴侣视为理所当然，或被迫为一个愚蠢的老板工作——很容易执着于这样的立场：解决这个问题不是你的工作，而这样做将是承认过错。但这里存在混淆。例如，如果我在家门口发现一个新生儿，这不会是我的过错，但它肯定是我的责任。会有选择要做，而且无法避免，因为试图忽略这件事本身就是一个选择。关键在于，门阶上婴儿的情况在所有情况下都适用：即使对方100%错误，长期来看，以此作为逃避责任的借口也毫无益处。

paragraphs.text: Should you find yourself on the receiving end of this kind of complaining, there's an ingenious way to shut it down—which is to agree with it, ardently. Psychotherapist Lori Gottlieb describes this as "over validation". For one thing, you'll be spared further moaning, since the other person's motivation was to confirm her beliefs, and now you're confirming them. But for another, as Gottlieb notes, people confronted with over-validation often hear their complaints afresh and start arguing back. The notion that they're utterly powerless suddenly seems unrealistic—not to mention rather annoying—so they're prompted instead to generate ideas about how they might change things.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你发现自己成为这种抱怨的接收方，有一种巧妙的方法可以制止它——那就是热情地同意它。心理治疗师洛里·戈特利布称之为“过度验证”。一方面，你将免受进一步的抱怨，因为对方的动机是确认她的信念，而现在你在确认它们。但另一方面，正如戈特利布指出的，面对过度验证的人常常会重新听到自己的抱怨并开始反驳。他们完全无力的想法突然显得不切实际——更不用说相当烦人——因此他们反而被促使去产生关于如何改变事情的想法。

paragraphs.text: "And then, sometimes, something magical might happen," Gottlieb writes. The other person "might realise she's not as trapped as you are saying she is, or as she feels." Which illustrates the irony of the responsibility/fault fallacy: evading responsibility feels comfortable, but turns out to be a prison; whereas assuming responsibility feels unpleasant, but ends up being freeing.
paragraphs.translation: “然后，有时，可能发生一些神奇的事情，”戈特利布写道。对方“可能意识到她并不像你所说的那样被困住，也不像她感觉的那样。”这体现了责任/过错谬误的讽刺：逃避责任感觉舒适，但结果是一座监狱；而承担责任感觉不愉快，但最终是自由的。

questions.questionText: What is characteristic of a chronic complainer, according to psychiatrist Eric Berne?

options.label: A
options.text: They only feel angry about their ill treatment and resent whoever tries to help.

options.label: B
options.text: They are chronically unhappy and ceaselessly find fault with people around them.

options.label: C
options.text: They constantly dismiss others' proposals while taking no responsibility for tackling the problem.

options.label: D
options.text: They lack the knowledge and basic skills required for successful conversations with their interlocutors.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段，Eric Berne 描述了一种被称为 'Why Don't You—Yes But' 的对话模式，其中慢性抱怨者会不断地抱怨他们的关系、工作或其他情况，但会找借口拒绝任何提出的解决方案。因此，C选项 'They constantly dismiss others' proposals while taking no responsibility for tackling the problem' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项中 'only feel angry' 和 'resent whoever tries to help' 过于绝对，文章没有提到慢性抱怨者只感到愤怒或怨恨帮助他们的人。
wrongOptions.B: B选项 'chronically unhappy' 和 'ceaselessly find fault' 描述不准确，文章中提到的是慢性抱怨者抱怨他们的处境，而不是不断地找周围人的错。
wrongOptions.D: D选项中 'lack the knowledge and basic skills' 与文章内容无关，文章讨论的是慢性抱怨者的态度和行为，而不是他们的知识和技能。

questions.questionText: What does the author try to illustrate with the example of the newborn on one's doorstep?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: It is easy to become attached to the position of overlooking one's own faults.

options.label: C
options.text: People are often at a loss when confronted with a number of choices.

options.label: D
options.text: A distinction should be drawn between responsibility and fault.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章中通过新生儿的例子来说明责任和错误之间的区别。作者指出，即使新生儿出现在门口不是作者的错，但作者有责任去处理这个问题。这个例子用来说明即使别人100%错了，逃避责任也不是长期的解决办法。因此，D选项 'A distinction should be drawn between responsibility and fault' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项 'People tend to think that one should not be held responsible for others' mistakes' 与文章内容不符，文章强调即使不是自己的错，也有责任去处理问题。
wrongOptions.B: B选项 'It is easy to become attached to the position of overlooking one's own faults' 没有提到，文章讨论的是责任和错误的区别，而不是忽视自己的错误。
wrongOptions.C: C选项 'People are often at a loss when confronted with a number of choices' 与文章内容无关，文章没有提到人们在面对多个选择时感到迷茫。

questions.questionText: What does the author advise people to do to chronic complainers?

options.label: A
options.text: Stop them from going further by agreeing with them.

options.label: B
options.text: Listen to their complaints ardently and sympathetically.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask them to validate their beliefs with further evidence.

options.label: D
options.text: Persuade them to clarify the confusion they have caused.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到，面对慢性抱怨者，一个巧妙的方法是同意他们的观点，即 'over validation'。这样做可以避免进一步的抱怨，因为对方的动机是确认自己的信念，而你现在正在确认它们。因此，A选项 'Stop them from going further by agreeing with them' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: B选项 'Listen to their complaints ardently and sympathetically' 与文章建议的 'over validation' 方法不符，文章建议的是同意他们的观点，而不是热情和同情地听他们的抱怨。
wrongOptions.C: C选项 'Ask them to validate their beliefs with further evidence' 与文章内容不符，文章建议的是同意他们的观点，而不是要求他们用更多证据来证实他们的信念。
wrongOptions.D: D选项 'Persuade them to clarify the confusion they have caused' 与文章内容不符，文章没有提到说服慢性抱怨者澄清他们造成的混乱。

questions.questionText: What happens when chronic complainers receive over-validation?

options.label: A
options.text: They are motivated to find ingenious ways to persuade their interlocutor.

options.label: B
options.text: They are prompted to come up with ideas for making possible changes.

options.label: C
options.text: They are stimulated to make more complaints.

options.label: D
options.text: They are encouraged to start arguing back.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到，当慢性抱怨者得到过度验证时，他们会重新听到他们的抱怨，并开始反驳。他们突然意识到自己并非完全无能为力，这促使他们产生可能改变现状的想法。因此，B选项 'They are prompted to come up with ideas for making possible changes' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项 'They are motivated to find ingenious ways to persuade their interlocutor' 与文章内容不符，文章没有提到慢性抱怨者被激励去寻找说服对方的方法。
wrongOptions.C: C选项 'They are stimulated to make more complaints' 与文章内容相反，文章提到过度验证会促使他们产生改变现状的想法，而不是刺激他们提出更多抱怨。
wrongOptions.D: D选项 'They are encouraged to start arguing back' 虽然部分正确，但不如B选项全面，因为文章提到他们会开始反驳，但更重要的是他们会思考如何改变现状。

questions.questionText: How can one stop being a chronic complainer according to the author?

options.label: A
options.text: Analysing the so-called responsibility/fault fallacy.

options.label: B
options.text: Avoiding hazardous traps in everyday social life.

options.label: C
options.text: Assuming responsibility to free oneself.

options.label: D
options.text: Awaiting something magical to happen.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到，逃避责任感觉舒服，但最终会变成监狱；而承担责任感觉不舒服，但最终会带来自由。因此，C选项 'Assuming responsibility to free oneself' 是正确答案，意味着通过承担责任来解放自己。

wrongOptions.A: A选项 'Analysing the so-called responsibility/fault fallacy' 虽然文章讨论了责任和错误的区别，但并没有提到分析这个谬误是停止成为慢性抱怨者的方法。
wrongOptions.B: B选项 'Avoiding hazardous traps in everyday social life' 与文章内容无关，文章没有提到避免日常生活中的危险陷阱。
wrongOptions.D: D选项 'Awaiting something magical to happen' 与文章内容不符，文章没有提到等待奇迹发生。

questionGroups.sourceText: 港珠澳大桥(Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge)全长55公里，是我国一项不同寻常的工程壮举。大桥将三个城市连接起来，是世界上最长的跨海桥梁和隧道系统。大桥将三个城市之间的旅行时间从三小时缩短到30分钟。这座跨度巨大的钢筋混泥土大桥充分证明中国有能力建造创纪录的巨型建筑。它将助推区域一体化，促进经济增长。大桥是中国发展自己的大湾区总体规划的关键。中国希望将大湾区建成在技术创新和经济繁荣上与旧金山、纽约和东京的湾区相媲美的地区。

answer.modelTranslation: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, spanning 55 kilometers, is an extraordinary engineering feat in our country. The bridge connects the three cities and is the world's longest sea-crossing bridge and tunnel system. It has reduced travel time between the cities from three hours to just 30 minutes. This massive steel-reinforced concrete bridge fully demonstrates China's capability to construct record-breaking megastructures. It will promote regional integration and stimulate economic growth. The bridge is key to China's development plan for its own Greater Bay Area, with aspirations to rival the bay areas of San Francisco, New York, and Tokyo in terms of technological innovation and economic prosperity.
